sources.authors: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer
sources.scope: Freshly read printed pages 243-252, browser lines 7253-7561: divisibility, division theorem, integer linear combinations, jug preservation, Euclid and the complete Pulverizer coefficient example. The historical modular-arithmetic pages are not claimed as freshly reread.
sources.qualifications: The positive numerical gcd definition excludes the zero pair. The chapter supplies its own computational extension. Positive-divisor remainder hypotheses are retained. A jug invariant alone proves necessity, not attainability; a move construction requires an additional argument.

sources.authors: Course notes; individual authorship of this edition has not been verified
sources.scope: All eight pages of Note 6 and all four pages of Note 7 were actually read through the official browser-accessible PDFs, including the extended-gcd trace, CRT coordinate construction, Fermat proof, RSA prime-coordinate proof and implementation discussion.
sources.qualifications: The archived Spring 2022 host is inaccessible in this revision. These are Fall 2026 notes, not newly obtained 2022 bytes. Zero divides zero under the existential divisibility convention. The division theorem requires positive, not merely nonzero, modulus for the stated remainder interval. Distinct primes and positive encryption/decryption exponents are explicit in the lesson. Historical parameter and security assertions are not adopted. Arithmetic operation count is distinct from bit cost.

sources.course: 15-151 Mathematical Foundations for Computer Science, Fall 2022
sources.scope: All 72 modular-arithmetic slides, browser lines 0-701, freshly read in overlapping ranges, including valuations, divisor coordinates, Gaussian congruence proof, linear-congruence fibers, Wilson, rotations and generalized CRT.
sources.qualifications: The Gaussian congruence proof needs the reduced difference b-pm, not the original b, as the smaller positive representative. Statements about primality algorithms are not imported as current claims. Two 60-bit operands can require a 120-bit product; 64-bit storage alone is insufficient for multiplication. The final Euclidean quotient need not be one. Generalized CRT sufficiency receives an independent proof.

sources.scope: Physical pages 123-143 and 151-182: all 14345 extracted characters freshly read in overlapping slices 0-7500 and 6800-end. Modular rings, inverses, positive division, common divisors, Euclid and coefficient tracing are covered.
sources.qualifications: Blank classroom proof slides do not constitute supplied complete proofs. Signed inputs, zero pairs and modulus-one conventions are independently reconciled. An unmatched parenthesis in the coefficient trace is not reproduced.

lessonReading: The complete lesson, all forty tutorials, all seventy historical review rules and all forty-seven canonical bank stems/options were read. No download is equated with reading.
limitations: Source-derived exercises are independently worded and specifically attributed. No claim to reproduce every exercise in each entire course or to guarantee answers to arbitrary unseen examinations is made.
